name: Paradise Pink
lede: Paradise Pink is a strong, warm red-pink that our sources mark only as an obscure, novelty name, with no book or dated plate behind it.

sections.title: An obscure name, no documented coiner
sections.body:
Our color library flags Paradise Pink as an obscure, qualified or novelty name rather than one tied to a dated system, and who first used it is undocumented in the sources consulted here [1]. No book, plate or standard list in our concordance carries this exact pairing of words for this hue [1].

The nearest named color by measured distance is [[cerise]], about 3.7 units away, almost the same shade [2]. [[red-plum]] and [[red-plum]] sit a little further out, both duller; [[pink-red]] and [[pink-red]] read more vivid [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: No painting in our archive of 23,781 paintings carries this color covering at least one percent of its canvas, within CIEDE2000 4 of the swatch, as photographed [3]. That describes the limits of this archive's photographs of aged, varnished paintings, not a judgment on where the color appears in life [3].
